beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:opening wide, hushed wonder]Almost ^every people on Earth tells of a great ^*flood*. [act:painting the map, wonder]From Greece to ^China, from the ^Andes to the islands of the ^Pacific, the water rises and the land ^disappears.
[d:tension][act:posing it, slowly]So is that ^one memory, passed from people to people... [act:letting it hang, softer][tune:fall]or ^many memories, of many ^floods?

[d:calm][act:plain, scholarly and warm]The oldest ^written versions come from ^Mesopotamia, the land between two rivers, in today's ^Iraq. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]Clay tablets, copied around {1650|sixteen fifty} BCE, tell the story of ^Atrahasis. [act:laying out the story's bones, one by one][tune:level]A hero is ^warned. [tune:level]He builds a ^boat. [tune:level]He releases ^birds to look for dry land. [tune:fall]And he makes a ^sacrifice.

[d:build][act:respectful, measured]Scholars note that Genesis tells its flood with the ^same bones. [act:with care, even-handed]And the ^Quran, too, remembers ^Nuh and his ^ark. [act:sincere, plain][tune:fall]Each tradition tells it in its own words, and for its own ^purpose.

[d:build][act:shifting gear, brisk]Now, let's look at the ^ground. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]In the last Ice Age, so much water was locked up in ice sheets that the seas stood far ^lower. [act:plain fact, a sense of scale]As the ice melted, the seas rose about a hundred and twenty ^metres and swallowed old ^coasts.

[d:build][go:3|0][sfx:shimmer][act:building, a little faster]And it didn't always rise ^slowly. [p:0.9][act:precise, the number]In one ^pulse, about fourteen and a half thousand years ago, the sea rose fourteen to twenty-five ^metres in a few ^centuries. [p:0.93][act:the comparison, vivid]Picture a building of five to eight ^storeys, made of ^water. [act:quieter, letting it sink in][tune:fall]Whole plains, gone within ^lifetimes.

[d:build][act:genuinely wondering][tune:rise]But can a story ^last that long? [act:explaining, warm]Without writing, a story survives only if each generation tells it to the ^next. [p:0.93][act:the answer, careful]In Australia, researchers matched twenty-one ^coastal stories to land that the rising sea really ^drowned... [count:7,000|years][act:the wonder of it, slower]remembered for over seven ^*thousand* years. [p:0.93][act:doing the sum, amazed]That's about two hundred and eighty ^generations, each one passing it ^on.

[d:reveal][act:weighing it up, generous]So the earth's own archives, its sediments and drowned shorelines, hold ^real floods. [act:building][tune:level]^Many of them. [act:building][tune:level]Some ^enormous: in North America, one ice dam burst forty times or ^more. [sfx:hit][p:0.93][act:the turn, clear and careful]What the layers don't show is ^one flood covering every land at ^once, in human times.
[d:aside][act:warm, gently curious]So a simple question ^stands. [act:warm, curious][tune:fall]For each ^local story, which real flood might lie ^behind it?

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Real floods behind ^some of these stories? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]^*Plausible*. [act:explaining, fair]The rising seas and the bursting ice dams are ^measured, and some stories fit them ^well. [act:the second weighing, even][tune:rise]^One shared origin for them all? [act:calm, precise][tune:fall]^Unproved.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:respectful, measured, sincere][tune:fall]What scripture ^tells is not what we ^rate: that belongs to ^faith. [act:gentle, a thoughtful pause]The ^water... [act:quiet, sure][tune:fall]the water we ^can measure.
